patch_description: The current program scores 0.00, which strongly suggests the optimizer gets stuck in degenerate (collinear) configurations — the lattice warm starts contain many collinear triplets with zero area, and the simulated-annealing acceptance rule (`val >= cur - T*1e-3*rng.random() or val > cur`) is non-standard and too permissive, letting the walk drift while the "best" snapshot may still be near-degenerate. Two targeted fixes inspired by standard best practice for the Heilbronn problem: (1) repair degenerate warm starts by adding jitter so every restart begins with a positive minimum area, and (2) replace the SA with a strict improving-move local search (move a vertex of the currently-worst triangle, accept only strict improvements with margin), wrapped in a best-of-many-restarts loop with an anytime time budget (~25s). Since the prior successful pattern (per the recommendation) was "more restarts of a proven search," and search quality varies across random starts, best-of-36 is the lowest-risk path to a higher score while keeping the deterministic seed for reproducibility.
